name: Azaziah
overview: Azaziah was a male Levite known specifically for his role as a lyre player, serving in the musical worship of Israel. His identity as a Levite situates him within the tribe set apart for service to God, particularly in the context of temple worship. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or activities beyond his musical service.
namesAndTitles: The name Azaziah means 'y-h-v-h is strong,' reflecting a declaration of God's strength. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:21, highlights a common biblical practice where names convey theological truths or attributes of God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Azaziah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple duties. No further family relationships are recorded beyond his tribal affiliation and role as a Levite musician.
scriptureSignificance: Azaziah's significance lies in his contribution to the worship of the Lord through music, specifically as a lyre player among the Levites. His role underscores the importance of skilled musicians in leading Israel's worship and honoring God in the temple. Though not extensively detailed, his mention affirms the biblical emphasis on dedicated service and the use of musical gifts in glorifying God.
